qt: to the Commission Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR) Subject:

The European wine sector contributes around EUR 130 billion to the EU’s GDP and supports almost 3 million direct and indirect jobs. In Greece, viticulture generates significant added value through vertically integrated production, processing and its links to gastronomy, wine tourism and cultural heritage. It contributes to the country’s overall tourism experience, creating sustainable jobs and strengthening social and territorial cohesion, particularly in island, mountainous and geographically disadvantaged areas. Despite recent EU initiatives in support of wine tourism and environmental adaptation, the proposed integration of the CAP into the National and Regional Partnership Plans after 2027 raises concerns about the continuation of dedicated funding for the sector. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Does it intend to ensure separate, earmarked funding for the wine sector and common European co-financing rates, regardless of national budgetary priorities?
How will it promote vertical integration, wine tourism, environmental adaptation and the creation of high-quality, sustainable jobs, making use of synergies between the CAP and cohesion policy?
Will it ensure access to support for individual winegrowers, wineries, cooperatives and other eligible entities, without making them solely dependent on recognised producer organisations?
